title: Ops Alchemy: Cross-team SLO Experiments (90-day incubator)
content:
Purpose:
This doc frames a 90-day incubator for small, high-velocity SLO experiments that require explicit cross-team coordination (SRE, Serving Runtime, Platform, Product-hosted-api, Observability). The goal is to quickly validate low-risk reliability levers, make them reproducible, and decide whether to productize them as part of the SLO program and operational guardrails.

Context and motivation:
- We need faster feedback loops for SLO interventions: throttles, dynamic batching, adaptive alert thresholds, and lightweight circuit-breakers.
- Many reliability improvements live in informal teams — this incubator formalizes a repeatable experiment pattern with clear success criteria, instrumentation templates, and handoff artifacts.
- Emphasis on low blast radius, measurable signal, and short feedback cycles.

Primary objectives (what success looks like in 90 days):
1) Run 3 independent experiments across different areas (networking, batching, and alerting) with observable impact on target SLO metrics.
2) Produce baked templates: dashboard widgets, alert config snippets, runbook checkpoint sections, and a one-page handoff to product/platform teams.
3) Commit at least one experiment to the service baseline (config + docs) and create a small rollout plan.

Hypotheses (examples):
- H1: Adaptive alert thresholds based on 95th percentile latency windows will reduce noisy paging by >=40% while keeping P95 alerts for regressions.
- H2: Short session-level KV cache warmups in the serving runtime reduce tail-latency for chat workloads by >=10% with no meaningful increase in GPU utilization.
- H3: A temporary, per-route request shed (soft-throttle) during queueing spikes preserves error budget across dependent downstream services.

Scope (in/out):
In-scope: host-api routes used by customer-facing chat endpoints, the serving-runtime batching layer, platform autoscaling hooks, and observability dashboards (datadog/grafana).
Out-of-scope: experiments that require model architecture changes, major infra re-architecting, or changes requiring >1 week of deep infra maintenance.

Phases & cadence:
- Week 0 (Prep): finalize experiment charters (one-pagers), assign owners, create tracking tickets (Jira REL-4xx), and pre-register dashboards.
- Weeks 1-4 (Discover & small-scale MVT): test experiments in staging with synthetic load, capture baseline signals, refine success metrics.
- Weeks 5-8 (Production-canary): run low-risk variants in production on narrow traffic slices (5–15%) with tight observability.
- Weeks 9-12 (Embed or kill): decide per experiment: embed as config + runbook, iterate, or terminate. Deliverables: templates and a handoff PR.

Weekly rituals:
- Monday 30m standup (sre-incubator): quick status, blockers, next steps.
- Wednesday deep-sync (1h): demo telemetry, discuss hypothesis drift, plan adjustments.
- Friday notes (async): short doc update + retrospective snippet.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Incubator Lead (Maya Chen): run cadence, coordinate cross-team interlocks, final decision maker for embedding.
- Experiment Owner (per-experiment): designs experiment, implements change, runs staging and canary. Expected: 0.2–0.4 FTE during active weeks.
- Observability SME (Noah Kim): dashboard + SLO measurement ownership, alert experiment setup, guardrail checks.
- Serving Runtime Engineer (Ethan Park): implements batching/KV variants and performance profiling.
- Platform/Infra Liaison (Aisha Rahman): provides access to canary routing, scaling knobs and assists with capacity tests.
- Product Partner (Sofia Alvarez): represents user impact, acceptance criteria, and prioritization.

Experiment templates (to be copied into each charter):
- Name, owner, start date
- Hypothesis and business impact statement
- Success metrics (primary SLO delta) and secondary signals (cpu/gpu%, queue length, error-rate)
- Planned staging steps and canary slice selection
- Rollback conditions and safety limits
- Dashboards and alert rule names
- Linked tickets and PRs

Three example experiments (short sketches):
1) Adaptive P95 alerting trial
- Owner: Noah Kim
- Idea: Replace fixed latency thresholds with sliding-window baselines that trigger when a short-term deviation >X sigma occurs and the error budget is low.
- Measure: paging rate, time-to-ack, false-positive rate, and missed regressions.
- Canary: 10% of internal test traffic, then 5% customer traffic.
- Rollback: re-enable fixed thresholds if missed regression rate increases by >10%.

2) Lightweight request-shed for downstream preservation
- Owner: Aisha Rahman
- Idea: Implement a probabilistic soft-throttle at ingress for overloaded routes to reduce cascading failures in downstream ranking/embedding services.
- Measure: downstream 5m error budget burn-rate, overall successful responses, customer latency.
- Safety: no more than 2% of requests lost for any user group.

3) Micro-batch tuning for chat sequences
- Owner: Ethan Park
- Idea: Increase micro-batch window by 15ms for select worker pools during predictable peak windows to improve GPU utilization and reduce per-token cost while monitoring tail-latency.
- Measure: per-token latency, P95/P99, GPU utilization, unit cost.

Telemetry & dashboards:
- Baseline capture: capture 7-day baseline for all experiment signals before canary.
- Dashboards: minimal 5-panel view (Traffic, P95, P99, Error-rate, Downstream error-rate). Use grafana link template: /d/expr/incubator-{experiment}.
- SLO measurement: continue to use the canonical SLO exporter (slo-exporter.redwood) so results are comparable.

Alerting policy iteration:
- Use non-pager experimental channels first (slack #sre-incubator) and then promote to pager if signals hold.
- All new experimental alerts must have a TTL and auto-disable after the canary window unless endorsed.

Runbook & incident integration:
- Each experiment must add a 2‑paragraph section to the canonical runbook: play, how to diagnose, and immediate rollback steps.
- Any incident during canary must surface to incident-review board and be evaluated against experiment rollback criteria.

Error budget governance and decision points:
- Establish a temporary error-budget policy for incubator slices: experiments may consume up to 5% of the global monthly error budget per service for the canary phase, subject to SRE review.
- Weekly review gating: if cumulative experiment consumption >8% of monthly budget for a dependent service, pause all experiments affecting that service.

Release gating and handoff artifacts (if embed decision):
- Merge PR with config change + unit tests + telemetry panels + runbook snippet.
- Product acceptance sign-off (Sofia).
- Small-step rollout plan: 5% → 25% → 60% → 100% with hold windows and automatic rollback hooks.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: noisy signals leading to premature kills. Mitigation: require 3 consecutive measurement windows before label change and encourage offline validation.
- Risk: shared resource contention (GPU). Mitigation: sched limits and capacity reservations for experiment slices.

Dependencies & blockers:
- Observability: must have exporter coverage for new metrics (ticket REL-491).
- Platform: canary routing feature flag needs a 2-week lead (PR #448).
- Legal/Compliance: experiments touching PII paths require product privacy review.

Comms plan:
- Weekly incubator note posted to #sre-incubator + short summary in Eng Weekly.
- Midpoint demo open to the Reliability Guild.
- Final one-pager in Confluence and a short demo during Eng All-Hands.

Success handoff checklist (if experiment embeds):
- PR merged with config, tests green
- Dashboard panels added to service baseline view
- Runbook updated with rollback steps
- Product sign-off and a rollout schedule in Jira
- Post-mortem / short experiment retrospective recorded

Open questions / decisions needed:
- How to quantify acceptable customer impact for request-shed experiments? (product input)
- Confirm permanent error-budget policy changes if an experiment is embedded.
- Who owns cost/finance signal when experiments interact with autoscaling?

Immediate next steps (this week):
1) Finalize three charters and create Jira REL-48x tickets (owners: Maya + experiment owners).
2) Noah to provision dashboard templates and pre-fill with baseline queries.
3) Platform to allocate a canary slice (Aisha) and ensure feature-flag gating.
4) Schedule kickoff demos in calendar: Monday standup + Wednesday deep-sync.

Appendix: quick templates (cut/paste)
- Dashboard panel queries (example): request_rate(), p95_latency(), p99_latency(), downstream_error_rate()
- Alert snippet (example): WHEN p95_latency(serviceX, 5m) > dynamic_threshold() AND error_budget_remaining(serviceX) < 15% -> notify #sre-incubator
- Runbook snippet template: Problem statement, immediate check (3 metrics), rollback action, follow-ups

Notes to self:
- Keep experiments short and reversible.
- Document every non-obvious decision in the incubator ticket.
- Avoid expanding scope mid-flight; use a follow-up project for larger wins.

(End of draft)
